title: [review] project-LICHEN-worker6-2729: protect_response missing request_kid identity validation
description:
In `protect_response` (lib.rs:975), after removing the `include_piv` parameter, the function no longer validates that `request_kid == self.recipient_id()`. The parallel `protect_response_with_reserved_piv` (lib.rs:1050-1053) correctly checks:
```rust
if request_kid.len() > NONCE_ID_LEN
    || OscoreSeqNum::from_piv(request_piv).is_none()
    || request_kid != self.recipient_id()
{
    return Err(OscoreError::InvalidParam);
}
```

The `protect_response` function (no-PIV path, RFC 8613 Section 5.2) should include the same validation. Passing a wrong `request_kid` silently produces a ciphertext that cannot be decrypted by the requester. Test `response_without_piv_requires_requester_identity` (lib.rs:3231) demonstrates this — it expected `InvalidParam` when `request_kid != sender_id`, but currently returns `Ok` because the check is missing.

RFC 8613 Section 5.2: the no-PIV response reuses the request nonce, but must bind to the correct requester. The request_kid must match the responders recipient_id (the requesters sender_id).

Fix: add the same three-checks guard from `protect_response_with_reserved_piv` to the top of `protect_response`, replacing or preceding the current `allow_no_piv_response` check.
